mainTopic: Eulogies, readiness for death, and the end of פרק שואל; then a traveler's pouch when שבת begins on the road
overview: The amud opens with the last words of a statement from the previous daf about the soul after death. רב teaches that a person's הספד shows whether he is a בן העולם הבא. The sign is whether the listeners are truly moved, and רבה adds that the tears of a few worthy scholars are enough. רבי אלעזר, רבי חנינא, and the people of the גליל and יהודה add more about who is a בן העולם הבא and how to earn good words at one's הספד. רבי אליעזר's teaching "repent one day before your death" means repent every day. A פסוק in קהלת and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's parable of the king's feast, along with רבי מאיר's sharper ending, teach the same lesson. After a second reading of the פסוק as ציצית and תפילין, פרק שואל ends. The new פרק teaches what a traveler does with his money pouch when שבת begins on the road. The גמרא explains this leniency, limits it to his own pouch, and ranks who should carry it: a גוי, a donkey, then a שוטה. The question of a חרש versus a קטן begins with a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The soul rises and does not come down again
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing line of a statement from the previous daf. After twelve months, the soul goes up and no longer comes back down.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his soul goes up, and it does not come down anymore.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that began on the previous daf. That statement describes what happens to the soul after death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full statement said that for the first twelve months after death, the body still exists and the soul goes up and down. After twelve months the body is gone, so the soul goes up permanently. This line is that final stage.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the tail end of a sentence from the previous daf (the twelve-month period after death), so do not read it as a standalone teaching.

phrases.english: And his soul ascends,
phrases.notes: After twelve months, once the body has decomposed.

phrases.english: and it does not descend anymore.
phrases.notes: It stays in its place under the Throne of Glory.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement from the previous daf (152b).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After twelve months, the soul ascends permanently and no longer descends.

steps.title: A הספד reveals whether a person is a בן העולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, says that you can tell from a person's הספד whether he is a בן העולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, said in the name of רב: From a person's הספד you can tell whether or not he has a share in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what a הספד shows about the person who died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that when the listeners are truly moved and brought to tears, it shows the person was righteous. The reaction of the crowd works as a kind of testimony about his life.

keyTerms.meaning: a person with a share in the World-to-Come

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said
in the name of Rav:
From a person's eulogy it is apparent

phrases.aramaic: אִם בֶּן הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא הוּא, אִם לָאו.
phrases.english: whether he has a share in the World-to-Come, or not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about eulogies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's eulogy reveals whether he is a בן העולם הבא.

steps.title: Challenge: רב himself asked for a moving eulogy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this can be true, since רב told רב שמואל בר שילת to make his הספד stir people's hearts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רב said to רב שמואל בר שילת: Make my eulogy moving, because I will be standing there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's statement using something רב himself said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the crowd's emotion depends on how skillful the speaker is, then it seems to prove nothing about the person who died. Even someone as great as רב asked the speaker to stir people up. That makes it look as if the reaction can be manufactured.

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav say to Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat:
Stir hearts during my eulogy,
phrases.notes: Literally 'heat up' the eulogy.

phrases.english: for I will be standing there!
phrases.notes: רב's soul would be present and listening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a eulogy reveals whether the person is a בן העולם הבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the speaker's effort determines the emotion, then the crowd's reaction cannot serve as a sign about the person who died.

steps.title: The sign is whether people are actually moved
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the speaker always tries to move the crowd. The sign is whether the crowd is actually moved or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. In one case they try to stir him and he is stirred; in the other case they try to stir him and he is not stirred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating the speaker's effort from the listeners' response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב asked for effort, and effort is always proper. The proof about the person who died comes from the result. If people are moved, he was righteous; if they are not moved despite the effort, that is a bad sign. So the two statements do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: that they try to stir him

steps.whatToRemember: The speaker's effort is not the sign. The real sign is whether the listeners are truly moved.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is where they stir him and he is stirred.
phrases.notes: A sign that the person was righteous.

phrases.english: That is where they stir him and he is not stirred.
phrases.notes: A sign that he was not.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דִּמְחַמּוּ לֵיהּ וְחָאֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two situations (effort vs. actual response)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a speaker can work up the crowd, the emotion seems to prove nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Effort is always made; the actual emotional response is what reveals the person's status.

steps.title: אביי asks who will cry for the disliked רבה
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה: since all the people of פומבדיתא dislike you, who will be moved at your הספד?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבה: Someone like you, master, whom all the people of פומבדיתא hate, who will be moved at your eulogy?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי applies the rule just taught to his own teacher, רבה, and asks a pointed question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sign is the crowd's emotion, then a great צדיק who is unpopular seems to be at a disadvantage. רבה was disliked because he rebuked the people of his city.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rabba:
In the case of the Master,
whom all the people of Pumbedita hate,
phrases.notes: Because he rebuked them.

phrases.english: who will be stirred at the eulogy?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַבָּה: כְּגוֹן מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 4 to a specific person.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the sign can work for an unpopular person.

steps.title: רבה: two worthy mourners are enough
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that it is enough for him if אביי and רבה בר רב חנן are moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is enough for me if you and רבה בר רב חנן are moved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is the reaction of worthy people, not the size of the crowd. If true תלמידי חכמים are moved, that is a meaningful sign, even if the general public does not care.
steps.whatToRemember: The reaction of a few worthy people matters more than the reaction of a large crowd.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מִיסָּתַאי אַתְּ וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן.
phrases.english: It is enough for me with you and Rabba bar Rav Ḥanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִיסָּתַאי אַתְּ וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The emotion of a few worthy scholars is enough to serve as the sign.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks who is a בן העולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks רב what kind of person is a בן העולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked רב: Who is a person with a share in עולם הבא?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is raised that sets up the next step: what marks a person as a בן העולם הבא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves from the specific sign of the הספד to a general question about how to identify such a person.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked Rav:
Who has a share in the World-to-Come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A definition or sign of a בן העולם הבא.

steps.title: רב answers with a פסוק: people say 'this is the path'
steps.stepSummary: רב answers with a פסוק: a person about whom people say, 'This is the way, walk in it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'And your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying: This is the way, walk in it, when you turn right or left' (ישעיה ל:כא).
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers רבי אלעזר's question by quoting a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Behind you' refers to what people say after a person dies, at his הספד. If they hold him up as a model and say 'follow his path,' that shows he is a בן העולם הבא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
"And your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying:
This is the path, walk on it,
when you turn to the right or to the left."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 30:21

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאׇזְנֶיךָ תִּשְׁמַעְנָה דָבָר מֵאַחֲרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One whom people praise after his death as a model to follow.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: one whom the Rabbis are pleased with
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא gives another sign: anyone the חכמים are pleased with is a בן העולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Anyone with whom our Rabbis are pleased.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא offers a different answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of looking at what people say at the הספד, רבי חנינא looks at the approval of the חכמים during the person's life. This fits רבה's point that the judgment of scholars is what counts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Anyone with whom our Rabbis are pleased.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: כׇּל שֶׁדַּעַת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ נוֹחָה הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the question of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן העולם הבא is someone the חכמים are pleased with.

steps.title: גליל and יהודה describe הספד customs differently
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'the mourners go about in the marketplace,' the people of the גליל say 'do deeds in front of your bier,' and the people of יהודה say 'behind your bier.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the mourners go about in the marketplace' (קהלת יב:ה). The people of the גליל say: Do things in front of your bier. The people of יהודה say: Do things behind your bier.
steps.whatsHappening: Two groups give different sayings about the הספד. This sets up the question of whether they disagree, which the next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sayings mean the same thing: live in a way that gives the speakers good things to say at your הספד. The only difference is where the speakers stand, in front of the bier or behind it.

phrases.english: "And the eulogizers walk about the marketplace",
phrases.notes: קהלת 12:5

phrases.english: The people of the Galilee say:
Do things that will be said in front of your bier,
The people of Judea say:
Do things that will be said behind your bier.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבְבוּ בַּשּׁוּק הַסּוֹפְדִים, בְּנֵי גָלִילָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the eulogy theme with a new פסוק and two sayings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Live so that good things will be said at your eulogy (phrased two ways).

steps.title: No real disagreement: each follows his local custom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the two groups do not disagree. Each is describing the custom of its own region.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree: each master spoke according to the custom of his own place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the apparent dispute from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the גליל, the speakers walked in front of the bier; in יהודה, they walked behind it. Both sayings carry the same message, adjusted to local practice.
steps.whatToRemember: The גליל and יהודה give the same lesson; only the local הספד custom differs.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
this Master according to his place,
phrases.notes: In the Galilee, eulogizers walked before the bier.

phrases.english: and this Master according to his place.
phrases.notes: In Judea, they walked behind it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי: מָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ, וּמָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reconciles the two sayings in step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גליל and יהודה seem to disagree about the eulogy.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each describes the custom of its own region; the message is the same.

steps.title: Repent one day before you die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere: רבי אליעזר says, do תשובה one day before your death.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: רבי אליעזר says, repent one day before your death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching from another משנה that connects to the theme of preparing for death. רבי אליעזר tells a person to do תשובה one day before he dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last steps discussed doing good deeds before death. This statement adds a specific instruction: do תשובה before your last day. The wording sounds odd on purpose, and it sets up the students' question in the next step.

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishna):
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Repent one day before your death.
phrases.notes: משנה אבות 2:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of preparing for death from the 'before your bier' discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should do תשובה one day before his death.

steps.title: The students ask how anyone can know his day of death
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's students ask him: does a person know which day he will die?
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבי אליעזר: Does a person know on which day he will die?
steps.whatsHappening: The students point out the obvious problem: nobody knows when he will die, so how can he repent 'one day before'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question meant to understand the teaching, not an attack on it. The question opens the door for רבי אליעזר to explain what he really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it so that... (introduces a surprised question)

phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Eliezer:
But does a person know
on which day he will die?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the instruction in step 12 can be carried out
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a person repent one day before death if he does not know when he will die?

steps.title: Repent today, so your whole life is spent in תשובה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers: all the more so. Repent today in case you die tomorrow, and then your whole life will be spent in תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: All the more so! He should repent today, in case he dies tomorrow. That way, all his days are spent in repentance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר explains that this was exactly his point. Since you don't know when you will die, you should repent every single day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students' question is not a problem for the teaching. It is the reason for it. The words 'one day before your death' really mean 'every day', because any day could be the last one.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Repent one day before your death' really means: repent every day, because any day could be your last.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is not telling you to wait until near the end. The instruction is a clever way of saying you must always be ready.

phrases.english: He said to them: All the more so,
let him repent today, lest he die tomorrow,
and it turns out that all his days are in repentance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because you don't know your day of death, you should repent daily, and then your whole life is spent in תשובה.

steps.title: שלמה המלך's פסוק: always keep your clothes white
steps.stepSummary: Support from קהלת: 'At all times your clothes should be white, and oil should not be missing from your head.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And שלמה also said in his wisdom: 'At all times your clothes should be white, and oil should not be missing from your head.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from שלמה המלך that teaches the same idea: always be prepared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White clothes and oil on the head are a picture of being clean and ready. Being ready 'at all times' matches רבי אליעזר's point about doing תשובה every day.

keyTerms.meaning: Your clothes white (a picture of being pure and ready)

phrases.english: And Solomon too said in his wisdom:
"At all times let your clothes be white,
and let oil not be missing from your head."
phrases.notes: קהלת 9:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 14 with a פסוק
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a person must always be ready, through daily תשובה

steps.title: The parable: a king invites his servants without setting a time
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי tells a parable. A king invited his servants to a feast with no set time. The wise got dressed and waited at the door. The fools went back to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said: It is like a king who invited his servants to a feast but did not tell them when. The wise ones dressed up and sat at the entrance of the palace. They said: Is anything missing in the king's house? (The feast could start any minute.) The fools went to their work. They said: Can there be a feast without a lot of preparation? (It will surely take a while.)
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי begins a parable to illustrate the same lesson. This step sets up the story; the outcome comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king is ה׳, the feast is the עולם הבא, and the unknown time is the day of death. The wise reason that the king can call at any moment. The fools assume there is plenty of time. This matches the two attitudes toward תשובה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said:

phrases.aramaic: מָשָׁל לְמֶלֶךְ שֶׁזִּימֵּן אֶת עֲבָדָיו לִסְעוּדָה,
phrases.english: A parable: to a king who invited his servants to a feast,
and did not set a time for them.
The wise among them adorned themselves
and sat at the entrance of the king's house.
They said: Is anything lacking in the king's house?
phrases.notes: Meaning: everything is ready, so we could be called any moment.

phrases.english: The fools among them went to their work.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ סְעוּדָה בְּלֹא טוֹרַח?
phrases.english: They said: Is there a feast without effort?
phrases.notes: Meaning: preparing takes time, so we have time to spare.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי: מָשָׁל לְמֶלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the idea of being ready at all times with a parable
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must live as if he could be called before ה׳ at any moment.

steps.title: The king calls suddenly: the ready ones eat, the unready ones stand
steps.stepSummary: The king suddenly calls his servants. The wise come in dressed up and the fools come in dirty. The wise sit, eat and drink. The fools must stand and watch.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suddenly the king called his servants. The wise ones came in dressed up, and the fools came in dirty. The king was happy with the wise and angry with the fools. He said: Those who dressed up for the feast, let them sit and eat and drink. Those who did not dress up, let them stand and watch.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the parable. The call comes without warning, and each group is treated according to how ready it was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'suddenly' is the key: death comes without notice. The prepared enjoy the עולם הבא. The unprepared are present but left out, which shows the cost of putting off תשובה.
steps.whatToRemember: In the parable, the call comes 'suddenly'. The ones who were always ready enjoy the feast, and the ones who delayed are left out.

phrases.english: Suddenly the king called for his servants.

phrases.aramaic: פִּיקְחִין שֶׁבָּהֶן נִכְנְסוּ לְפָנָיו כְּשֶׁהֵן מְקוּשָּׁטִין,
phrases.english: The wise among them entered before him adorned,
and the fools entered before him dirty.
The king rejoiced to greet the wise
and was angry to greet the fools.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: הַלָּלוּ שֶׁקִּישְּׁטוּ אֶת עַצְמָן לַסְּעוּדָה —
phrases.english: He said: These who adorned themselves for the feast,
let them sit and eat and drink;
these who did not adorn themselves for the feast,
let them stand and watch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the parable begun in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those prepared enjoy the feast; those unprepared must stand and watch.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: standing would just look like serving
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר's son-in-law, quoting רבי מאיר, objects to the parable's ending: if the fools stand, they would simply look like waiters, which is not much of a punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר's son-in-law said in the name of רבי מאיר: They too would look like they are serving.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר finds a weakness in the ending of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's parable. People standing at a feast look like servants on duty, so they are not embarrassed. This sets up his new version of the ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The target is only the punishment in the parable, not its main lesson. Standing near the table is not shameful enough to show how serious it is to be unprepared.

phrases.aramaic: חֲתָנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir's son-in-law said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
They too would look like attendants (serving the meal).

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲתָנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ending of the parable in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The ending 'let them stand and watch'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Standing servants look like waiters, so the punishment is not shameful enough.

steps.title: Both groups sit, but only the ready ones eat and drink
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר's version: both groups sit at the table. The ready ones eat and drink, and the unready ones stay hungry and thirsty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both groups sit. These eat and those are hungry. These drink and those are thirsty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives his own ending to the parable. Everyone sits at the table, but the unprepared get nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting at a full table while unable to eat is far more painful and shameful than standing to the side. This makes the cost of not preparing in this world much sharper.

phrases.english: Rather, these and those both sit:
these eat, and those are hungry;
these drink, and those are thirsty,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the ending that step 18 found too mild
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The unprepared would stand and watch, looking like waiters.
steps.terutzMaskana: The unprepared sit at the table hungry and thirsty while the prepared eat and drink.

steps.title: Proof from ישעיהו: My servants eat and you go hungry
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר supports his version with a פסוק in ישעיהו: My servants will eat and you will be hungry, drink and you will be thirsty, sing with joy and you will cry out in pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'So says ה׳: Behold, My servants will eat and you will be hungry. Behold, My servants will drink and you will be thirsty. Behold, My servants will sing from a happy heart, and you will cry out from a pained heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר brings a פסוק that describes exactly his picture: two groups side by side, one enjoying and one suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places both groups together and contrasts eating with hunger and drinking with thirst. That matches 'both sit, these eat and those are hungry' rather than one group standing off to the side.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: Two endings to the parable: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says the unprepared stand and watch. רבי מאיר says everyone sits, but the unprepared stay hungry and thirsty, based on ישעיהו. Both teach the same lesson: be ready every day through תשובה.

phrases.english: as it is said: "Thus says the Lord:
Behold, My servants shall eat, and you shall be hungry;
behold, My servants shall drink, and you shall be thirsty;
behold, My servants shall sing from a glad heart,
and you shall cry out from a pained heart."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 65:13–14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the פסוק that supports רבי מאיר's ending in step 19
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's ending: both sit, but only the prepared eat and drink

steps.title: A second reading: white clothes are ציצית, oil is תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another explanation of the פסוק in קהלת: white garments refer to ציצית, and oil on the head refers to תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'At all times let your clothes be white' refers to ציצית. 'And let oil not be missing from your head' refers to תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different reading of the same פסוק that was used for the parable about always being ready.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading treated 'white clothes' as a picture of always being ready, like the wise servants who were dressed and waiting. This דבר אחר reads the פסוק as pointing to two specific מצוות: white garments are ציצית, and something worn on the head is תפילין. The message of being 'dressed for the King' now becomes concrete: keep doing these מצוות constantly.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation; a second, different reading of the same source
Ritual fringes on a four-cornered garment
Leather boxes with parchment, worn on the head and arm

steps.whatToRemember: פרק שואל ends with a call to readiness: always be dressed for the King, both in spirit (repentance) and in actual מצוות (ציצית and תפילין).

phrases.english: Another explanation:
'At all times let your clothes be white'
phrases.notes: קהלת ט:ח

phrases.english: these are ציצית,
phrases.notes: Fringes are white and are worn on clothing.

phrases.english: 'and let oil not be missing from your head'
these are תפילין.
phrases.notes: Like oil, תפילין are placed on the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative reading of the קהלת פסוק quoted in step 15, which was first read as a general call to always be ready (as the parable in steps 16-20 illustrated).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק hints at constantly wearing ציצית and תפילין.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק שואל
steps.stepSummary: The formal closing formula for פרק שואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק שואל.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter. The next step starts a brand-new פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is not part of the argument. It is a traditional farewell that shows love for the learning and a commitment to come back to it. Anything after this line belongs to a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula said when finishing a פרק
The name of the chapter being closed (פרק כ״ג of שבת)

phrases.english: We will return to you, [chapter] Sho'el

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after its final אגדה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק שואל is complete. A new chapter begins.

steps.title: Caught on the road at nightfall: give the pouch to a non-Jew or put it on the donkey
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that someone still traveling when שבת begins gives his money pouch to a גוי. If no גוי is with him, he places it on his donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone for whom it became dark (שבת started) while he was on the road gives his pouch to a גוי. If no גוי is with him, he puts it on the donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens. The משנה deals with a traveler who is still carrying his money when שבת begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He cannot carry the pouch himself, because carrying four אמות in a רשות הרבים is forbidden. The משנה gives a ranked solution. The first choice is to hand it to a גוי. Only if there is no גוי does he load it onto his donkey, which suggests the donkey option is considered less preferable.

keyTerms.meaning: It became dark for him; שבת began

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume handing something to a גוי on שבת is normally fine. The very next steps of the גמרא question why it is allowed here.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One for whom it became dark on the road,
phrases.notes: שבת began while he was still traveling.

phrases.english: gives his pouch to a non-Jew,
and if there is no non-Jew with him,
he places it on the donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A traveler at nightfall should first give his pouch to a גוי. If no גוי is present, he places it on his donkey.

steps.title: Arriving at the outer courtyard: unloading the donkey
steps.stepSummary: When he reaches the outer courtyard, he takes down items that may be moved on שבת. For items that may not be moved, he unties the ropes and lets the bags fall by themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reaches the outer courtyard, he takes off the items that are allowed to be moved on שבת. For the items that are not allowed to be moved on שבת, he unties the ropes, and the sacks fall on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the same case and explains what to do with the donkey's load once he reaches a safe, enclosed area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The outer courtyard is a protected place where his belongings are secure. Items that are permitted to be handled (not מוקצה) he may simply lift down. Items that are מוקצה he may not lift. Instead, he unties the ropes so the load drops by itself, which relieves the animal without his directly moving the מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer courtyard, the first enclosed area at the edge of town
May be moved on שבת (not מוקצה)

phrases.english: Once he reached the outer courtyard,
he takes the items that may be moved on Shabbat.
And those that may not be moved on Shabbat,
he unties the ropes,
and the sacks fall (on their own).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's case from the road to arrival at a secure place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Permitted items are removed by hand. For מוקצה items, he unties the ropes so they fall by themselves.

steps.title: Why were the רבנן lenient about giving the pouch to a non-Jew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's permission to hand one's pouch to a גוי on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the רבנן allowed him to give his pouch to a גוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for the reason behind the משנה's first ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, having a גוי do a forbidden מלאכה for a Jew on שבת (אמירה לגוי) is not allowed. Here the גוי will carry the pouch for the Jew. So the גמרא wants to know why חכמים made an exception in this case.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason
that the Rabbis permitted him
to give his pouch to a non-Jew?
phrases.notes: Here's the problem: אמירה לגוי, asking a non-Jew to do it for you, is usually forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind the first ruling of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for permitting something that looks like forbidden אמירה לגוי.

steps.title: People won't abandon their money, so a smaller leniency prevents a bigger sin
steps.stepSummary: חכמים know that a person will not give up his money. If they did not permit handing it to a גוי, he would carry it four אמות in a רשות הרבים himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן know that a person does not hold himself back when his money is at stake. If you do not allow him this, he will end up carrying it four אמות in a public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: חכמים allowed a lighter, rabbinic leniency in order to prevent a Torah-level violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking a גוי to carry is only an איסור דרבנן. Carrying four אמות in a רשות הרבים is an איסור דאורייתא. Because people panic about losing money, חכמים relaxed their own rule so the person would not come to break the Torah prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: They are certain; it is established for them

keyTerms.term: אֵין אָדָם מַעֲמִיד עַצְמוֹ עַל מָמוֹנוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A person does not restrain himself when his money is at stake
Four cubits, the distance whose carrying in public is forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic principle: חכמים may relax a rabbinic rule to prevent a person from violating a Torah prohibition, especially where money loss would push him to sin.

phrases.english: The Rabbis are certain

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין אָדָם מַעֲמִיד עַצְמוֹ עַל מָמוֹנוֹ,
phrases.english: that a person does not restrain himself regarding his money,
if you do not permit him,
he will come to carry four cubits
in the public domain.
phrases.notes: A Torah prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: קִים לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דְּאֵין אָדָם מַעֲמִיד עַצְמוֹ עַל מָמוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of why the leniency was given.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because people will not abandon their money, חכמים allowed handing the pouch to a גוי (a rabbinic matter) to prevent carrying four אמות in a רשות הרבים (a Torah prohibition).

steps.title: רבא limits the leniency to one's own pouch
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the permission to hand items to a גוי applies only to one's own כיס, not to a מציאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Only his own pouch may be given to a גוי, but not a found object.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets a limit on the משנה's leniency. Only a person's own money pouch may be handed to a גוי, not something he found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the leniency was that a person will not give up his own money (Step 26). A מציאה is not money he worked for, so he can bear to leave it behind. That means the reason for the leniency does not apply to it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Specifically his pouch,
but a found object — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the leniency explained in Step 26 to the case it was designed for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one's own כיס may be handed to a גוי; a מציאה may not.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious from the משנה's wording?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's statement as obvious, since the משנה itself says 'his pouch'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious? We learned in the משנה 'his pouch'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that רבא's ruling adds nothing. The משנה already says 'כיסו', his pouch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is that רבא's statement is unnecessary (פשיטא). If the משנה names a specific item, then other items are naturally excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious,
we learned 'his pouch'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבא's statement in Step 27 is needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says 'כיסו', so excluding a מציאה seems obvious and not worth stating.

steps.title: The משנה might have just been using a common example
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought 'כיסו' was only the typical example, and that a מציאה is included too. רבא teaches that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said the same rule applies even to a found object, and the משנה said 'his pouch' only because that is the usual case. So רבא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. Without his statement, we could have thought the משנה just used a common example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes a משנה names the usual case without meaning to exclude others (אורחא דמילתא). רבא tells us that here the word 'כיסו' is precise, so a מציאה is really excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: The usual way things happen; a typical example

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying the משנה's wording is loose. The answer says we might have thought so, and רבא teaches that the wording is exact.

phrases.english: You might have said
the same law applies even to a found object,
and the fact that it teaches 'his pouch' —
it teaches the usual way of things,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא הוּא הַדִּין אֲפִילּוּ מְצִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of Step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Justifies the need for the statement by naming a reasonable mistaken assumption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כיסו' is just a typical example, so a מציאה would also be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כיסו' is precise; a מציאה is excluded.

steps.title: A found object already in his hands counts like his pouch
steps.stepSummary: The exclusion of a מציאה applies only when it has not yet come into his hands. Once it is in his possession, it is treated like his כיס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said this when the found object has not come into his hand. But if it came into his hand, it is like his pouch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to רבא's limit. A מציאה he already picked up gets the same leniency as his own pouch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a found object is actually in his hands, he feels it is his. He would be just as unwilling to give it up as his own money. So the reasoning of Step 26 applies again.

keyTerms.meaning: It is considered like his pouch

steps.whatToRemember: In this first version: his own כיס may go to a גוי. A מציאה not yet in hand may not. A מציאה already in hand is like his כיס.

phrases.english: And we only said this
where it did not come into his hand,
but if it came into his hand —
it is like his pouch.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא דְּלָא אֲתַי לִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies רבא's exclusion of a מציאה in Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מציאה already in one's possession is treated like one's כיס and may be handed to a גוי.

steps.title: Second version: רבא asks about a found object in his possession
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבא asks a question about a מציאה that came into his possession. Is it like his כיס because he holds it, or not, because he did not work for it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבא asked: What is the law of a found object that came into his possession? Since it came into his hand, is it like his pouch? Or perhaps, since he did not work for it, it is not like his pouch?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version. Here, what was a clear ruling in Step 30 is recorded as an open question (בעיא) from רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides. Holding it might make him attached to it like his own money. On the other hand, since he did not work for it, he could more easily let it go. In that case חכמים would have no need to allow handing it to a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not put effort into it

phrases.english: Some say,
Rava asked:
a found object that came into his hand, what is the law?
Since it came into his hand —
is it like his pouch?
Or perhaps
since he did not exert himself for it —
it is not like his pouch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the clear ruling of Step 30 into an unresolved question in a second version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מציאה already in one's possession has the status of one's כיס for the leniency of handing it to a גוי.

steps.title: The question remains unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question is left without an answer: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends רבא's question without deciding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether holding a מציאה makes it like one's own money. So in this version, the case of a מציאה already in hand stays doubtful.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in Step 31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the second version, the status of a מציאה already in one's possession remains a doubt.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה: a gentile comes before the donkey
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's words 'אין עמו גוי', the גמרא infers that if a גוי is present, he must give the pouch to the גוי rather than put it on the donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'there is no gentile with him.' The reason he puts it on the donkey is that there is no gentile with him. But if there is a gentile with him, he gives it to the gentile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and draws an inference from its wording. This sets up the next question: why is a גוי better than a donkey?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows the donkey only when no גוי is there. That shows the donkey is a second choice, and a גוי is preferred when one is available.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no gentile with him
The reason is because (introducing an inference)

phrases.english: 'There is no gentile with him.'
The reason is that there is no gentile with him,
but if there is a gentile with him —
he gives it to the gentile.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאֵין עִמּוֹ גּוֹי, הָא יֵשׁ עִמּוֹ גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רבא's discussion to the next phrase of the משנה (Step 23).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a גוי is present, the pouch is given to the גוי rather than placed on the donkey.

steps.title: Why is a gentile preferred over a donkey?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a גוי is preferred over a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the order it just inferred. It is setting up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have thought a donkey is better, since it is only an animal and not a person. So the preference for a גוי needs an explanation.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the inference in Step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a גוי takes priority over one's donkey.

steps.title: We are commanded about a donkey's rest, not a gentile's
steps.stepSummary: A Jew is commanded about the rest (שביתה) of his donkey on שבת, but not about the rest of a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A donkey — you are commanded about its rest. A gentile — you are not commanded about his rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers. Loading one's own donkey touches on the Torah command that one's animal must rest. Giving the pouch to a גוי does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah commands that one's animal must rest on שבת (שביתת בהמה). There is no such command about a גוי. So handing the pouch to a גוי is the lighter choice.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the principle behind the ranking: choose the option that involves the least Torah prohibition.

phrases.english: A donkey —
you are commanded about its rest,
a gentile —
you are not commanded about his rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah commands the rest of one's animal (שביתת בהמה) but not the rest of a גוי, so the גוי is preferred.

steps.title: A donkey comes before a deaf-mute, imbecile, or minor
steps.stepSummary: If the choices are a donkey, a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן, he places the pouch on the donkey and does not give it to any of the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: A donkey and a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor: he places it on the donkey. He does not give it to the deaf-mute, the imbecile, or the minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another ranking for when no גוי is present. The donkey is preferred over these people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן are not obligated in מצוות. Still, the גמרא prefers the donkey over them. The reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute (treated as lacking full legal understanding)

phrases.english: A donkey and a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor —
he places it on the donkey,
to the deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor
he does not give it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ranking from Steps 33-35 to the case where no גוי is present.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A donkey is preferred over a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן.

steps.title: Why is the donkey preferred over these people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the donkey takes priority over a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ranking it just gave. This sets up the short answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising after Step 35. There, we learned that we are commanded about a donkey's rest. That might suggest people who are not obligated in מצוות should come first.

keyTerms.meaning: Commandments (which a חרש, שוטה, and קטן are not obligated in)

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in Step 36.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a donkey takes priority over a חרש, a שוטה, or a קטן.

steps.title: They are people; the donkey is not
steps.stepSummary: A חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן are still people. Other people of their kind are obligated in מצוות, so someone might confuse them. A donkey is not a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are people; this one is not a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that being human is what matters here. It is worse to have a person carry than an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though they are not obligated in מצוות, other people of their kind are obligated in מצוות. Someone might confuse them and come to give the pouch to a person who is obligated. A donkey cannot be confused this way.

phrases.english: These — are people,
this one — is not a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חרש, a שוטה, and a קטן are people, while a donkey is not, so the donkey is preferred.

steps.title: The imbecile is preferred over a deaf-mute or a minor
steps.stepSummary: Between a חרש and a שוטה, he gives it to the שוטה. Between a שוטה and a קטן, he also gives it to the שוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A deaf-mute and an imbecile: to the imbecile. An imbecile and a minor: to the imbecile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ranks the people among themselves. The שוטה is the preferred choice in both pairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שוטה has the least legal understanding of the group. So having him carry is the least like a real person doing מלאכה. This sets up the open question of a חרש versus a קטן that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Legal understanding (the factor behind the ranking)

steps.whatToRemember: The order of preference is: גוי, then חמור, then שוטה, and only after that a חרש or a קטן.

phrases.english: A deaf-mute and an imbecile —
to the imbecile.
An imbecile and a minor —
to the imbecile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ranking from Steps 36-38 among the people themselves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שוטה is preferred over a חרש and over a קטן.

steps.title: Which comes first: a deaf-mute or a child?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the only choices are a חרש and a קטן, which one should get the pouch?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: a חרש and a קטן, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has ranked every other pair, so it now asks about the one pair still missing: a חרש versus a קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 39 we learned that a שוטה comes before a חרש and before a קטן. That ruling does not tell us how a חרש and a קטן compare to each other. The question is really about which of the two counts as 'less of a person' who acts with understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was asked of them." The formula that opens a real question in the בית מדרש.
A deaf-mute, who in הלכה is treated as lacking full understanding (דעת)
A minor, a child below the age of מצוות
"What?" Here it means "what is the law?"

phrases.english: They asked:
A deaf-mute and a minor, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Meaning: if only these two are available, to whom does he give the pouch?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the last missing comparison in the ranking that step 39 began.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a חרש or a קטן comes first for carrying the pouch.

steps.title: According to רבי אליעזר there is no question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the question: according to רבי אליעזר the answer is already clear.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, you do not need to ask.
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering fully, the גמרא says the question only applies to one opinion. According to רבי אליעזר, the answer is already known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line limits the scope of the question. Whatever the doubt is, it does not exist for רבי אליעזר, because he has a clear view of a חרש's mental status. The proof for this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: "You need not ask." The case is already clear.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer to the whole question. It only says the question has an obvious answer according to רבי אליעזר. The question may still stand according to other opinions.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer
you need not ask,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Partly answers step 40 by showing that the question is already settled for one opinion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי אליעזר the question is already settled. The source follows.

steps.title: Proof begins: a ברייתא about a חרש's תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא in which רבי יצחק reports רבי אליעזר's ruling about the תרומה of a חרש. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יצחק says in the name of רבי אליעזר: the תרומה of a חרש...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its proof for step 41 by quoting a ברייתא. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To know how רבי אליעזר views a חרש, the גמרא looks at a different area of law: whether a חרש can separate תרומה. Separating תרומה requires intention and understanding. So רבי אליעזר's ruling there will show how much understanding he thinks a חרש has, and that will decide the comparison with a קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce set aside for a כהן, which requires intention to separate

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא often learns how a person's mental status works in one area, here שבת, from how it works in another area, here תרומה. The common thread is whether the person has דעת.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
Rabbi Yitzchak says
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
the terumah of a deaf-mute,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that supports the claim in step 41.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי אליעזר the comparison between a חרש and a קטן is clear.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יצחק quotes רבי אליעזר about the תרומה of a חרש (continued on the next amud).
